newsitem.title: USA: Pan Am expects to begin flights Sept. 26.
newsitem.headline: Pan Am expects to begin flights Sept. 26.

text.p: The new Pan American World Airways, which was granted final Department of Transportation certification Wednesday, said Thursday it plans to begin service Sept. 26.
The Pan Am name returns to the skies for the first time since the original debt-laden airline collapsed in 1991.

Florida businessmen Chuck Cobb and Martin Shugrue bought the Pan Am name and logo in 1993 with the plan of eventually resurrecting the carrier, which had been one of the commerical aviation industry's pioneers.
Shugrue previously served as vice chairman and chief operating officer of the old Pan Am.

Pan Am, with headquarters located near Miami International Airport, will fly wide-body Airbus Industrie A-300 aircraft in daily flights between New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport and both Los Angeles and Miami.

"We have worked long and hard to make this day a reality," said Shugrue. "The travelling public worldwide celebrates the return of one of the most respected names in air travel -- and we are committed to uphold this unique position."
Pan Am's merger with Frost Hanna Mergers Group Inc. became effective with the Transportation Department's final certification.

The carrier received regulatory approval despite a petition by the families of victims killed in the 1988 Pan Am Flight 103 explosion over Lockerbie, Scotland. The families opposed Shugrue's involvement with the carrier.
The new Pan Am said it will attempt to stimulate demand by offering affordable pricing.

The carrier said that contrary to industry practice, it will not impose Saturday night stay-over requirements or advance purchase restrictions. The airline also said it will not charge fees to change non-refundable tickets.
The airline said it will have a simplified fare structure, with all seats in each class of service available at the same price during the introductory period lasting until Nov. 24.
